report.tagline: A London AI company that turns a script into a training video with a realistic AI presenter, in 140+ languages, without cameras or studios.
report.simpleSummary: Synthesia lets companies make videos without filming. You type a script, pick an AI presenter (an avatar that looks and talks like a real person), and in a few minutes you get a video. The same video can be turned into dozens of languages. Most customers are big companies making staff training, onboarding and product how-to videos.

overview.whatItDoes: Synthesia is a web app for making videos with AI presenters. It is used mainly for training, internal communication, sales enablement and customer education. It replaces filming with a script editor, so updating a video means editing text, not reshooting.
howItWorks: Pick a template or start from a document, PowerPoint or web link; the AI drafts a script and scenes.
Choose from 240+ stock avatars or create a personal avatar of yourself from a short recording.
The avatar reads the script with lip-sync, gestures and natural voice in 140+ languages.
Add screen recordings, images and quizzes; some plans make interactive videos.
Translate the whole video in one click and keep every language in sync when the script changes.
Share by link, embed, or export to learning systems used by HR teams.
overview.valueProposition: Professional training videos in minutes, in every language your staff speak, at a fraction of the cost of filming.

businessModel.summary: Synthesia sells software subscriptions. Small users pay monthly self-serve plans with a set number of video minutes. Most revenue comes from Enterprise contracts with large companies, priced by seats, minutes and features like custom avatars and security.

revenueStreams.detail: Annual contracts with large companies; likely the majority of revenue.
Starter (about $29 a month) and Creator (about $89 a month) with video minute limits.
Studio or personal avatars, included in some plans or charged extra.
Generate videos programmatically for personalised outreach and product videos.

businessModel.pricing: Free plan with limited minutes. Starter about $29 a month. Creator about $89 a month. Enterprise: custom. Yearly billing is cheaper. Prices from synthesia.io and may change.
costDrivers: GPU compute to generate video, which is far more expensive than text
Research on avatar and voice models
Enterprise sales and customer success teams
businessModel.unitEconomics: A big company might pay $50,000 to $500,000 a year. Making a 5-minute video might cost Synthesia a few dollars in compute. Compared with an agency charging $5,000 or more per filmed video, customers save a lot, and Synthesia keeps a healthy margin. Self-serve users paying $29 a month are profitable on compute, but many churn after a project. Enterprise retention is the real money maker.

howTheyGetUsers: Free demo video on the website with no sign-up
Enterprise sales targeting HR and training teams
Content marketing and SEO for 'AI video generator' searches
Customers sharing videos that show Synthesia's quality
Partnerships with learning systems and video tools
whatBringsUsersBack: Training needs never end; content must be updated
Personal avatars and brand kits saved in the account
Video libraries in many languages to maintain
growth.moat: Synthesia's moat is enterprise trust plus a focus on training. Big companies have approved it through security and legal checks, built libraries of videos and personal avatars, and connected it to their learning systems. Switching means redoing all of that. Avatar quality alone is not a moat, since rivals like HeyGen and Google improve fast.

northStar.metric: Minutes of Synthesia video watched by viewers each month
northStar.why: Videos only create value when people watch them. Watched minutes capture both customer creation and real audience impact, which helps renewals. As a north star metric, it beats videos made, because unwatched videos deliver nothing. Guardrail metrics make sure growth does not come at the cost of trust, safety or margins.

pmLessons: Pick a boring but valuable use case. Training videos are not flashy, but companies pay well and keep paying.
Enterprise trust can beat raw tech. Security and consent rules win big buyers.
Updates matter more than creation. Editing text instead of reshooting is a big reason customers stay.
Translation multiplies value. One video in 20 languages is worth much more than one.
Know your threats. Big tech bundling free tools is the main risk for focused startups.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you defend Synthesia against Google Vids being free in Workspace?
interviewQuestions.hint: Identify what Synthesia does better: avatars, languages, training features, security. Focus on enterprise training needs. Measure win rate and churn.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the right north star for Synthesia?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare videos made, minutes generated and minutes watched. Argue for watched minutes and break into creation, translation and engagement.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce churn among self-serve users?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why they leave: one-off projects, price, limits. Ideas: pay-as-you-go, templates, reminders. Track month 2 retention.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Synthesia handle the risk of avatars being used for misinformation?
interviewQuestions.hint: Consent rules, content checks, watermarks, banning political content, clear reporting. Balance safety with ease of use.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature that helps sales teams use Synthesia.
interviewQuestions.hint: Personalised videos per prospect using the API. Define workflow, data sources and success metric like reply rate.
